llm_brief.text:
Core: A short poem about rare clouds, ending with a question (the user's words). Choose one rare formation and its light or edge, then write a poem that turns and ends on a question about something the poem has shown.
Also relevant: Nacreous clouds form in the winter polar stratosphere, about 15 to 25 km up, and glow with pastel, iridescent colour near twilight. Noctilucent clouds are higher and shine after sunset. Kelvin-Helmholtz clouds are rippled bands like breaking waves, with capped crests and clear troughs. Mammatus clouds are pouch-like bulges hanging under a cloud base. Asperitas is a rough, turbulent sheet. A fallstreak hole is a round or oval gap in a supercooled cloud layer. Name the cloud by its visible shape and light. Put a turn (a but, yet or however, or a change of image) before the last stanza.
Say instead: for clouds, say the visible shape or movement, not 'ethereal', 'whispering' or 'dancing'. For the close, end on an image or a question, not a moral. For the question, ask about a detail the poem has shown, not 'what does it mean?'.
Open: Form, length, stanza count, rhyme and tone are not fixed by the prompt. Short is one reading among a few stanzas of short lines, one breath, or a turn that fits a couplet.
Options: one cloud up close or a sky with two formations; a single closing question aimed at the reader, the cloud, or left open; rhymed or unrhymed short lines.

ak-what-does-it-mean.instead: a question the poem asks the cloud or the reader's glance, left open in the last line

ak-cloud-mood.excluded_sense: a mood or fog of feeling (a cloud over someone)
ak-cloud-mood.instead: a physical cloud with shape and light

ak-rhyme-padding.instead: a rhyme only where it carries the turn; otherwise short unrhymed lines

ak-generic-cloud.instead: one named rare formation (lenticular, nacreous, mammatus, fallstreak hole) seen in its light

ak-long-poem.instead: a few short stanzas with one image and one turn

ak-cloud-cliche.instead: a concrete colour, edge or shape for the cloud; a plain verb such as hangs, thins or holds for what it does

ak-closing-moral.instead: end on the image or the question; the last line states no lesson

ak-noise-stunning.instead: name the one visible detail that makes the cloud striking

k-question-last.text: The final line is a question, ends with a question mark, and nothing follows it.

k-rare-subject.text: The poem is about rare clouds, not clouds in general: at least one formation is named by its shape or its light.

test.spec: name the rare formation the poem shows; a poem of only generic cloud words fails

k-short.text: The poem reads as short in one of its readings: a few stanzas of short lines, one breath, or a turn that fits a couplet. Stanza count is not fixed.

test.spec: the poem could be read in one breath or in a few short stanzas, and does not run on as a long poem

k-formation-matches-facts.text: The formation the poem names matches the shape or light given for it in the facts entries (nacreous, noctilucent, lenticular, Kelvin-Helmholtz, mammatus, asperitas, fallstreak hole).

test.spec: the named cloud's visible shape or light agrees with its entry; a shape from another formation fails

k-no-cloud-cliche.text: No stock cloud word appears in the poem.

k-no-moral.text: The closing line does not state a moral or lesson.

test.spec: the last line shows an image or asks a question; it does not state what the cloud teaches

k-no-what-does-it-mean.text: The final question is not 'what does it mean?' or a near variant.

test.spec: what does it mean\? must not match the last line

k-concrete-image.text: Each stanza carries at least one concrete visible detail (shape, colour or edge).

test.spec: each stanza names a thing that could be seen

k-light-specific.text: The formation's light is specific: a named colour or edge on the cloud, not generic brightness.

test.spec: a colour or edge word sits on the cloud itself

k-turn.text: A turn (a but, yet or however, or a change of image) appears before the last stanza.

test.spec: the speaker's attention shifts before the final stanza

k-question-target.text: The question points at something the poem has shown (the cloud's light or shape), not at a general idea.

test.spec: the question names a visible detail from earlier lines

craft._about: Discipline primer for poetry and verse craft, and nature poetry about sky and weather. Principles and craft habits, not a finished poem.

craft-concrete-image.text: A concrete image is a tangible, sensory detail: something seen, heard or touched, not an abstraction.
behaviors: A cloud named by its visible shape and light carries more than the word cloud
An abstract noun in the image slot gives the reader nothing to see
craft-concrete-image.principle: The reader feels the thing before the feeling; the image does the naming.
signals: a noun with colour, edge or shape
no abstract noun in an image line

craft-turn.text: The turn (volta) is a rhetorical shift that marks a change of thought in the poem, often waking the reader to a different meaning.
behaviors: A sky description turns when the speaker's glance lands on one cloud
A turn can be a single 'but', 'yet' or 'however', or only a change of image
craft-turn.principle: A short poem needs a change before its end, and the turn gives the last line something to land on.
signals: a but, yet or however
the scene moves from sky to speaker

craft-closing-line.text: The closing line carries the turn and one image together, and stops before explaining either.
behaviors: End on the cloud's last visible detail, not on what the cloud means
The final line can be the question itself, with nothing after it
craft-closing-line.principle: Stop before the explanation; the reader takes the last step.
signals: last line is an image or a question
no line after the question mark

craft-common-mistakes.text: Short poems weaken through stock cloud imagery, a closing moral, and over-explaining the image after showing it.
behaviors: A last line that states the lesson closes the image
Explaining how a cloud forms after showing it spends the reader's attention twice
craft-common-mistakes.principle: Show the rare cloud once, clearly, and let the reader carry it out.
signals: ethereal, whispering or dancing for clouds
a final line that states a moral

craft-economy.text: Economy in a short poem can be read as a few stanzas of short lines, as one breath, or as a turn that fits in a couplet. In each reading a line earns its place by adding one new thing.

readings.in_practice: three to four stanzas, each line carrying one image
signals: stanza count stated by shape
each line adds one new thing

readings.in_practice: a single stanza read in one exhale, cut to what the reader can hold at once
signals: under about twelve lines
no stanza break needed

readings.in_practice: the shift in thought fits in the last two lines
signals: turn and close share a couplet

craft-question-ending.text: A question ending can aim at the reader, at the cloud, or stay open. The target decides what the reader carries out.

readings.in_practice: the cloud becomes a shared glance, the reader is asked whether they have seen it
signals: 'you' in the final line
a visible detail of the cloud named in the question

readings.reading: question the poem asks the cloud
readings.in_practice: the speaker and the formation stay in the frame, and the cloud is asked what it will do
signals: the cloud addressed directly
a visible detail of the cloud named in the question

signals: question mark is the last character
the question names something on the page

readings.in_practice: a question about what the cloud means, detached from the image
signals: 'what does it mean' or similar
no visible detail in the question

rare_clouds_facts._about: Researched rare formations and vocabulary; lite depth, two fetched pages.

rare-nacreous-conditions.term: where and when nacreous clouds form
rare-nacreous-conditions.text: They form in the winter polar stratosphere, about 15 to 25 km up, where the air is extremely cold.
behaviors: The stratosphere is usually too dry for cloud, so these are uncommon
Sightings in Britain are unusual
signals: reports of aurora that turn out to be cloud

rare-noctilucent.text: A higher, night-sky cousin of nacreous clouds that forms in the mesosphere and shines in early evening.
behaviors: Their greater height lets them catch sunlight after the lower clouds have gone dark
signals: glow in the evening after sunset, not at twilight low on the horizon

vocab-nacre.text: The name nacreous comes from nacre, another name for mother-of-pearl, so people also say mother-of-pearl clouds.
signals: pearly, shifting pastel tones
colour that looks like a sheen, not a rainbow

vocab-iridescence.text: People describe the colour as iridescent, and the mechanism is diffraction of sunlight by tiny ice crystals.
behaviors: Sunlight scatters off the crystals in different directions, so many colours appear at once

rare-nacreous.text: Rare winter clouds of the polar stratosphere that glow with iridescent colour near twilight.
behaviors: Colour appears close to sunset or before dawn, when the sun is just below the horizon
Ice crystals only a few micrometres across diffract the light
The same ice crystals also speed up the breakdown of the ozone layer, a hidden stake behind the beauty
rare-nacreous.principle: Their rarity comes from the cold: the stratosphere has to drop to extreme temperatures before they form.
signals: pastel pink, green and blue patches
wispy cirrus-like shape by day

rc-kelvin-helmholtz.text: Rippled cloud bands that look like breaking ocean waves, with capped crests and clear troughs.
behaviors: Wind flowing up and over a barrier such as a mountain sets up the wave pattern
Evaporation and condensation make the crests cloud and leave the troughs clear
rc-kelvin-helmholtz.principle: Two air layers moving at different speeds curl into waves, and the moist crests show as cloud.
signals: wave rows in a cloud layer
one band of cloud with clear gaps

rc-mammatus.text: Pouch-like bulges hanging under a cloud base, formed by sinking air rather than rising air.
behaviors: Sinking air forms them, reversing the usual upward cloud growth
Low sun lights the pouches from the side and makes them most visible
Rarity is not stated in the fetched pages
rc-mammatus.principle: Descending air shapes the cloud's underside into hanging pouches, so the cloud base reads as uneven.
signals: bulges on the underside of a cumulonimbus anvil
pouches framed by low sunlight

heading_path: Asperitas: Our new cloud became official in March 2017

rc-asperitas.text: A chaotic, rough-looking sheet of cloud with a turbulent surface; a supplementary feature in the WMO cloud atlas.
behaviors: Members sent photographs of it to the Cloud Appreciation Society, which proposed it as a classification in 2008
The WMO Atlas lists it as a supplementary feature of altocumulus and stratocumulus
rc-asperitas.principle: A cloud counts as a formal type only once a standard body names it; asperitas was named from citizen photographs.
signals: rough, churning underside of a cloud layer
named in the Cloud Appreciation Society library

rc-fallstreak-hole.text: A round or oval hole punched in a supercooled cloud layer, made when ice crystals start a chain reaction.
behaviors: Ice crystals grow at the expense of nearby droplets, which evaporate and leave the hole
A passing aircraft is a reasonable explanation for the formation, per meteorologists quoted by the page
rc-fallstreak-hole.principle: Freezing spreads through supercooled droplets and clears a gap, so the hole grows from one point.
signals: clean circular gap in a thin cloud layer
streaks trailing from the hole edge

rare-quality.text: 'Rare' in a poem about clouds can mean an uncommon form, an unusual light, or an uncommon occurrence. Each reading takes a different exemplar.

rare-ex-form-lenticular.text: A lens- or saucer-shaped cloud that stays fixed over high ground while the wind passes through it. Not checked against a fetched source.
properties: fixed over a ridge or peak
behaviors: It holds its place while the air under it moves
Its edge looks drawn on
rare-ex-form-lenticular.principle: The form is the rarity: the outline stays still while everything else moves.
transfers_to_poem: a cloud that does not drift
a shape the speaker can name by its edge

rare-ex-light-nacreous.text: Pearl-coloured polar clouds that glow when the sun is just below the horizon.
properties: pastel pink, green and blue patches
behaviors: Colour shows near dusk or before dawn, low on the horizon
Ice crystals split the light into bands of colour
rare-ex-light-nacreous.principle: The light is the subject; the cloud is the surface it crosses.
transfers_to_poem: the last colour before it fades
a glow that appears only low in the sky

rare-ex-light-noctilucent.text: A higher cousin of nacreous clouds that shines after the sun has gone down for the lower sky.
behaviors: Catches sunlight after the lower clouds have gone dark
rare-ex-light-noctilucent.principle: Height gives it a light the rest of the sky has already lost.
transfers_to_poem: a cloud lit after everything else is dark
a glow with no sun in view

rare-ex-occurrence-polar.text: The stratosphere is usually too dry for cloud, so these form only in extreme winter cold far north or south. Sightings in Britain are unusual.
behaviors: The wait is part of the rarity
A sky that is usually empty can suddenly hold one
rare-ex-occurrence-polar.principle: Rarity here is about conditions: the cloud appears only when the cold is extreme.
transfers_to_poem: a long wait for one winter dusk
a speaker who is the only one looking up

a cloud's shadow on a bare field

img-carry-without-naming.term: images that carry a cloud without naming it
img-carry-without-naming.text: Concrete visible details that let the reader see a cloud without the word cloud appearing in the line.
properties: a lens-shaped plate over a peak
a rolled edge like breaking surf
a white thread over a bare ridge
behaviors: A named shape and colour carries the cloud; the word cloud can stay out of the line

no abstract noun in the image slot

rhythm-quiet.term: rhythm for a short quiet poem
rhythm-quiet.text: Short lines with plain words, long open vowels and pauses that let an image settle.
properties: short lines of three to six words
a pause before the last line
no rhyme forced by the subject
behaviors: A line break before the final image makes the question land alone
rhythm-quiet.principle: Quiet comes from slow stresses and few words, not from soft adjectives.
signals: lines under eight syllables
a one-word or one-clause last line

avoid-cloud-cliches.text: Stock sky words that read as filler in a poem about clouds; swap each for a visible detail.
behaviors: A cloud that dances is a verb doing no work; name the movement or shape instead
avoid-cloud-cliches.principle: A stock word gives the reader a mood they already had; a concrete detail gives them the cloud.
signals: abstract verb on a cloud
fabric or veil metaphor with no edge

light-words.text: Light words that carry the look of nacreous and iridescent cloud without explaining the physics.
behaviors: Glow pairs with an edge: light sits on the cloud's rim, not across its whole body
light-words.principle: One light word per image keeps the colour specific; stacked light words blur it.
signals: one colour word per line
light placed on an edge or underside

ff-opt-stanza-shapes.text: Three shapes to try: three quatrains of short lines, two couplets then one question line, or a single stanza of seven to nine lines.

A turn in stanza one reads as a second opening
ff-turn.principle: The change of thought comes early enough for the last image to carry it.
signals: a but or yet opens the penultimate stanza
the speaker's eye lands on one formation
